title: The kit and the estate
dek: Work that belongs to no single archive: the shared components, the build gates, and anything that has to be true in all of them at once.

rows.what: Force-push the four rewritten histories
rows.note: Four public repositories were tracking raw family exports — a GEDCOM holding 134 people born since 1950, a tree export marking 137 alive. The rendered pages were clean throughout; the exposure sat one level below them. They are untracked and ignored now, the histories rewritten and verified, mirrors kept. **Pushing is irreversible, so it stops at a human.**

rows.what: Ask GitHub Support to purge the unreferenced objects
rows.note: A force-push rewrites the branch; it does not drop the old blobs. Until Support purges them they stay reachable by anyone who knows a commit hash. Follows item 1.

rows.what: Keep a worklist.json, so this board stops being written by hand
rows.note: Nine of ten archives now keep one, all calling the kit's gate rather than a forked copy, and every row of the 186 carries an owner and a date. The children's site is the exception and arguably should be — it is written for a six-year-old, not a research register. Adopted in about an hour, from one archive to nine.

rows.what: All thirteen Falco places carry n=0
rows.note: Nothing to size a dot by or rank a name by, so that archive has no front-page place picture while five others do. A data fix, not a component fix.

rows.what: Arienzo appears twice in D'Arcy's atlas, and it is a Falco parish
rows.note: n=12 and n=2 at identical coordinates, under /places/arienzo/ and /places/arienzo-2/. May be real — two of Falco's living people are in D'Arcy's tree — but duplicated under two slugs it is a fault either way. **18 place names in D'Arcy appear more than once**; Brisbane ×3, Averham ×3.

rows.what: Ten Blazevic place names appear more than once
rows.note: Senj ×3, Krivi Put ×3, Otočac ×2 — the same place under variant spellings, splitting its people between entries. The front-page picture now labels only the first of a repeated name, which hides the symptom rather than fixing it. **Merging places on a name is the thing this estate refuses to do automatically**, so this is a human call per place.

rows.what: Branch data for the rivers diagram
rows.note: The component is in the kit and takes one prop. What is missing is a paragraph per node — where a branch was, in what year, and what the archive can actually show happened there. Derivable lanes with empty prose would be a confident drawing that says nothing. Booyzen, D'Arcy, Blazevic, Mazza, Lerena.

rows.what: Sovereignty data for the timeline
rows.note: Blazevic's file existed and was wired on 15 September. The other five need lanes of districts with bands of [from, to, regime, label]. Regime dates are public history; which districts matter, and what the family lived through, is the archive's own work.

rows.what: Which Ivan is which
rows.note: Only 1 of 8 spine generations matches a dossier on name and dates, and the dossier called ivan-defranceski is dated 1829–1895, neither of them. Two consecutive generations are both Ivan Defranceski. **Nobody can derive this** — it is a reading, not a join.

rows.what: Booyzen carries ancestors only — no siblings, so no aunts or uncles
rows.note: 26 people and no lateral kin, so the blood chart there draws a line rather than a family. D'Arcy had the same gap and its GEDCOM answered it mechanically.

rows.what: Join the kin across archives
rows.note: Hedviga on the Defranceschi spine founds the Blazevic archive; Cheryl Anne founds Lerena's; two of Falco's living are in D'Arcy's tree. Seven archives that are one family and cannot yet say so to each other.

rows.what: 151 of 368 menu links resolved a redirect before a page
rows.note: It was not two links, it was **151** — 67 of D'Arcy's 72, 50 of Falco's 54, 33 of Mazza's 40. These sites build in directory format, so a path without a trailing slash is a 301 before the page: a wasted round trip on every click, on most of the navigation, on most of the archives. Confirmed live before touching anything. **Zero redirecting menu links across all seven now**, and the link checker confirms none of the new paths is dead.

rows.what: Four archives have no About page at all
rows.note: Booyzen, Blazevic, Mazza and Lerena. Three of seven tell a reader what the archive is and who made it; four do not.

rows.what: Two tiles still carry a year rather than a count
rows.note: Blazevic's «1750, the earliest Blazevic birth year» and Mazza's «1697, the earliest year this archive reaches». Both measure reach rather than telling a story, which is why they were left — but the canon says six measures, and this is a judgement call that should be yours.

rows.what: One chart, six archives — PersonTree, Ptree and Pedigree consolidated
rows.note: Six archives drew one chart under three names. The kit draws the shape; each archive keeps what only it can say about the evidence.

rows.what: The bloodline chart turned on its side
rows.note: 25,008px wide against 616 tall. Generations are columns now; the same chart is 1,966 × 5,740 and fits a phone.

rows.what: Front pages end the same way, carry six measures, and teach the evidence words in the first screen
rows.note: established → numbers → missing → the ring, on all seven. Tiles counted at build time. Documented / Inferred / Family lore before the doors.

rows.what: The household explorer opens into the blood graph
rows.note: Joined on FamilySearch record ids, never on names — the key the data carried was a forename. 24 of the 43 households that stood in no chain now have a way through.

rows.what: The menu canon, applied to all seven and re-verified
rows.note: Seven archives carried the same seventeen shared pages in seven different orders. The canon fixes POSITION, never a URL — so no link anyone had shared stopped resolving. **165 items moved.** Start · Our line · The families lead; People & places, then Evidence, close. Re-read off the BUILT sites on 15 September: all seven still hold it exactly, including three where other sessions worked in the layout file all week. The surname keeps two homes on purpose — its own group on the three archives with more than one page for it, last under Our line on the four with exactly one — so the menu says how far the name has been worked instead of hiding it.

rows.what: The front-page read-across, and the eight-slot canon it produced
rows.note: Measured off the built index.html of all seven. Found the same four sections everywhere in seven different orders, a 3× spread in words, six to ten number tiles, and evidence chips on three of seven. Produced the canon the front pages now follow: hero, the rule with its chips, three doors, one real drawing, what this archive has established, the archive in numbers, what is still missing, the ring. **What is deliberately NOT standardised:** the hero sentence, door two, the cards, and every archive's own sections — the Senj 1943 page, the rebels' testimony, the inquest, the passport. The shape is shared; the material is not.

rows.what: The blood-relatives chart, on all seven
rows.note: Built on the claim that it was blocked for want of parent identifiers. It was not — I had checked the wrong file. `dossiers.json` had carried 200 parent links and 765 sibling links by slug, each with the provenance that established it, for as long as it had existed. Every line is drawn in the colour of its own evidence at the WEAKER grade of the two records behind it, so the picture never claims more than the archive does. Nothing is matched on a name: an edge exists only where a record names a slug.

rows.what: The standing estate record — thirteen phases since September
rows.note: The read-across that found the seven archives were one system: shared colour, five evidence words, a page canon, one tree model, and the eight-site disagreement read side by side. It also carried the day four public repositories were found tracking raw family exports with living people in them. **Its living-person rule is superseded:** initials-only became the Falco approach — name them, nothing more, anyone over eighty treated as deceased — and `checkliving.py` enforces it on all seven.

rows.what: The lessons that cost the most, kept because they will be paid for again
rows.note: **Repinning a git dependency by editing package.json and running npm install is a no-op** — npm keeps the locked commit, seven archives reported clean installs on the old kit, and `npm ci` then refuses when the two disagree. Name-matching once gave one Pietro five mothers. A scoped `<style>` on a big list page makes Astro stamp a cid on every element — 2.7MB on one archive. `content-visibility` needs the plain length declared before the `auto <length>` form. A check that cannot fail is not a check: a build loop printed exit=0 beside a stack trace because it read the wrong command's status.

rows.what: The front-page drawings, specified rather than left in a chat
rows.note: `kit/docs/front-page-drawings.md` holds the schema for the sovereignty timeline and the rivers diagram, the two strict shape rules that left one archive's file inert for weeks, and the reason the place picture draws no coastline. Kept in the repository beside the components, because a published page and a chat window are the two places a spec does not survive.

rows.what: Four pages sit in a different menu group depending on the archive
rows.note: `/australia` is under **Leaving** on one and **Our line** on another; `/brisbane` **Leaving** vs **People & places**; `/gallery/` **Evidence** vs **The work**; `/namesakes/` **People & places** vs **The work**. A reader who learns where something lives on one site should find it in the same place on the next. Each needs one decision, then it applies to all seven. `/name` is the deliberate exception and stays as it is.

rows.what: Six shared pages carry genuinely different names
rows.note:
Four of the original ten were only case or an article and are settled — the estate writes menu labels in sentence case (257 of 368, and every archive's own majority), so «What Changed» → «What changed», «Photograph These» → «Photograph these», «What We Cannot Close», «The Namesakes» → «Namesakes».

The six left are a decision about voice, not a tidy-up: `/people/` is **The People** on one archive and **Nine lives in full** on another; `/who/` is **Every Name** and **Everyone, a page each**; `/gallery/` is **Gallery** and **The Plates**; `/lines` is **The Lines** and **The Four Quarters**; `/married-in/` is **Married In** and **The families they married**; `/australia` is **Australia** and **Arrival, 1826**. Worth deciding whether a shared page keeps one name everywhere, or the archive's own voice wins.

rows.what: The front pages run 1,486 to 5,080 words
rows.note: A 3.4× spread. The structure is aligned now — same order, same slots — but Defranceschi carries two large diagrams and nearly 5,100 words where Mazza has one small drawing and under 1,500. That gap is **writing and data**, not layout, and closing it is each archive's own work rather than something to be evened out from outside.

rows.what: The seven front pages now run in one order, with the drawing framed the same way
rows.note: Two archives introduced their picture with a heading and a line on how to read it; five dropped a bare dot-plot in with a caption, which is why one read as dots in a void. All seven now go hero, the rule with its chips, three doors, one framed drawing, the archive's own sections, established, numbers, missing, the ring. Verified on the built pages. **The middle stays different on purpose** — it is the reason each site is worth reading.

rows.what: All 368 menu items compared, seven archives side by side
rows.note: 55 pages more than one archive carries, 185 unique to one. Only four sit in the wrong group and ten carry inconsistent names — both now rows of their own above. The 185 are listed rather than flagged: they are what makes each archive its own.

rows.what: Luwinski does not run the estate's main build gate
rows.note: Its package.json has **check:living** and **check:worklist** but no **check:kit** — so `checkarchive.py`, which catches dead links, broken anchors, a missing sitemap and pages nothing links to, has never run on that archive. Every other archive gates on it. One line in package.json: `python3 node_modules/@daviddef/archive-kit/kit/tools/checkarchive.py --dist dist`.

rows.what: Luwinski publishes an empty search index, so its search finds nothing
rows.note: `/searchindex.json` is published but empty. Found by running the gate above by hand — which is the argument for wiring it: this has been live and invisible, and the archive's search box returns nothing for every query.

rows.what: The work list has no way to notice a row that is missing
rows.note: Found by the Blazevic session, not by the gate. Five letters had been sent; four were on the list and each looked fine in isolation. The fifth — DAR Ispostava u Senju, the nil return that named the three doors the other three letters went through — was absent entirely, so the list showed four letters and hid the one that generated three of them. **checkworklist.py validates rows that exist and can never see one that does not.** It needs to count the list against something outside it: letters against `requests/sent/`, corrections against corrections.json, and so on. Same failure class as a register over-reporting what is outstanding, in the other direction.

rows.what: Some sessions adopted the work list without the step that keeps it honest
rows.note: The Blazevic session is the one to copy: it re-counts its own rows against the evidence on disk rather than trusting what it wrote. Sessions that only append rows will drift the way every hand-kept register in this estate has. The prompt should say to reconcile, not just to record.

rows.what: Audited whether the other archives group married-in families by surname
rows.note: Only **Falco** is at fault, and only because it is the one asserting a relationship it has not tested: its rule is «any surname in the tree that is not Falco», with no descent check. **Blazevic** groups by surname but gates membership on an ahnentafel number, so nothing is listed because of a name — 19 families, 45 proven ancestors, zero inflation. **Defranceschi** groups by surname correctly, because that archive's subject IS the name: it says outright that there is no single Defranceschi family and that the name was invented independently many times over. Mazza and D'Arcy list surnames as a census and claim nothing. The rule is not «never group by surname» — it is that the grouping must match what the archive is about.

rows.what: Falco now places a married-in family by descent, not by spelling
rows.note: The register asked «is this surname something other than Falco?», so **Mazza** sat on a Falco page with no Falco near it, while **Annecchino** and **Zampiello** — who married into the family without ever marrying the name — read the same as a stranger. Each person is now placed by descent: born a Falco or descended from one, married such a person, the family that person came from, or married into one of those. **15 carry the blood, 48 married one, 36 are such a family, 4 married into one of those, 0 reach it not at all.** No name matching anywhere in it. Living people, previously dropped from the marriages entirely, are now named with the relationship and nothing else, which took marriages from 152 to 196.

rows.what: A grave no longer reduces an archive's count of the living
rows.note: **Bucolo read «0 withheld» when three of its people were living.** The build subtracted one from the withheld count for every Nudgee burial of the surname — seven graves against three living women, so the count floored at zero. Matching the two lists on a name instead is no better and I tested it: it fires nowhere across 77 surnames, and the one near-miss, a Carmine Falco at Nudgee and a Carmine Falco alive today, is **two people**. The tree says who is living; a burial index keyed on a name cannot outrank it. The decrement is gone, both sets are shown, and the note on the page now says plainly that they have not been joined. Estate-wide withheld went 98 → 105.

rows.what: Present the descent categories on the page, then roll the merged page to all seven
rows.note: The data now carries `reach` and `reachCount` per family; the page still shows the old flat list. Rebuild `married-in.astro` around the four categories, merge it with `/marriages/` as the prototype showed — descriptions, collapsible name lists, links to people pages, provenance chips, metrics, living collapsed — and then **carry that same page to all seven archives**, which is the point of the exercise and the user's explicit ask. Each archive keeps its own rule for what «reaches the family»: Blazevic's ahnentafel gate and Defranceschi's name-is-the-subject are both correct as they stand and must not be flattened into Falco's descent test.

rows.what: One marriages page, the same shape, on all seven archives
rows.note: `/marriages/` everywhere, labelled **The Marriages**, built on a shared `Marriages.astro`. The component renders labelled groups and **asserts nothing about why they are groups**, because the archives disagree for good reasons and each is right about itself: **Falco** and **Mazza** place a family by descent (their subject is a family); **Defranceschi** and **Lerena** group by origin and by status (their subject is a name); **Blazevic** and **D'Arcy** gate on an ahnentafel number; **Booyzen** reads back the line it has already assigned to each person. Old addresses redirect: `/married-in` on Falco, Defranceschi and Blazevic, `/families` on Mazza.

rows.what: A numbered ancestor loses their ahnentafel number through lib/people.js
rows.note: `add()` merges the family record over the ancestor record, and **every member in families.json carries an explicit `ahn: null`** — so anyone who is both a numbered ancestor and a member of a family comes out of `byId` with no number. Found because grouping 13 families by the generation they enter the line put **all 13** in «not on the direct line» and the page still looked correct. The marriages page now reads the number from ancestors.json, which owns it, but **anything else reading `byId(...).ahn` has the same hole**. `p.ancestor` survives the merge and is safe.

rows.what: Only the Booyzen line is numbered; the ten lines that married in are not
rows.note: All 136 people on the Booyzen line carry a generation, 2 to 7. The other ten lines — **190 people, more than the name itself holds** — carry none, so they cannot be ordered by when they arrived. The page says so rather than hiding it. Worth deciding whether that is a gap to fill or a policy to state: a first attempt grouped by generation regardless and **silently dropped every line without a number**, rendering one family out of eleven on a page that otherwise looked entirely correct.

rows.what: Seven Mazza surnames cannot be reached from the family at all
rows.note: The new descent test returns **blood 14 · married 17 · kin 37 · second 49 · unconnected 7**. The seven are the useful output — they are in the archive and no parent, child or spouse edge connects them to the line — and they only appear because the rule is capable of returning no. Each is a thread to pull or a record to remove.

rows.what: Compared all seven navigations route by route
rows.note: **`/who/` — the page this estate agreed to call «Every Name» — is built and live on all seven and was in the menu on five.** Falco had renamed it from `/names/` and never added it; Booyzen never added it at all. Both had been reachable by URL and by search the whole time and invisible to anyone using the navigation. Also normalised: «What Changed»/«What changed» (four sites to two, lowercase wins and matches «Our line, drawn») and Booyzen's «The Documents» → «Documents». **Everything else that differs, differs on purpose:** `/lines/` is three different pages about three different things, Booyzen's `/namesakes/` really is about forenames, and the extra menu groups — D'Arcy's four, Blazevic's Documents and Origins, Defranceschi's «Go there», Lerena's «The work» — are local content, not drift. The shared spine is **Start · Our line · People & places · Evidence** on all seven, with «The families» on six.

rows.what: Compared all seven footers; one said nothing about living people
rows.note: **The Mazza archive holds 334 living people — the most in the estate — and its footer said nothing about them.** The rule itself was stated three ways across the seven: «named, name and relationship only», «appear by name only, no dates no places no photographs», and «excluded from this build». All seven run the same gate, `--policy named-bare`, which is *named and nothing more*. Six now carry one sentence; Booyzen and Blazevic add that they currently hold none. **D'Arcy is a real exception and now says so on purpose** — it drops living people at the boundary in `lib/people.js` before the data is written, so its build carries neither their dates nor their names, which is stricter than the estate rule. Also fixed: the D'Arcy footer claimed «one of six archives» and named five, two paragraphs below a ring that reads seven from the shared file; and the Blazevic footer linked `/corrections/` under «What changed», which is the menu's label for `/changes/`. Every footer now carries Sources · Method · Open questions · Corrections, with local extras kept.

rows.what: Two pages titled «What changed» and «What Changed»
rows.note: `/changes/` renders **What changed** and `/corrections/` renders **What Changed** — two different pages whose titles differ by one capital letter. Found while aligning the footers, because the footer linked one of them under the other's menu label. The footer link now reads «Corrections», so nothing points the wrong way any more, **but the two page titles are still a coin-flip for a reader** and for anything that lists titles. One of them needs a different name.
